title: Build pipeline: YAML -> .gdt data-type archive generator (Gradle task)
description: Per gib.1.2 review decision (struct source of truth, option 3 from the start): a Gradle build task with Ghidra jars on the classpath walks the descriptor/types YAML and emits a .gdt data-type archive via FileDataTypeManager.createFileArchive(). The loader consumes ONLY the .gdt (standard archive API, no YAML parser in runtime). Rules: .gdt is a build artifact — never committed, never hand-edited, CI always regenerates. Deliverables: (a) YAML->DataType builder (structs, flags/enums, field comments); (b) Gradle task wiring; (c) generated c64ref-derived struct YAML for VIC-II/SID/CIA feeding it (or stub until the c64ref generator lands). Bonus: the .gdt doubles as a standalone publishable artifact usable in stock Ghidra.

title: Design: memory map schema and system descriptor format
description: Design the data model that describes a game system architecture: ROM regions (cart, BIOS), RAM regions, IO port ranges, mirroring rules, initial data type definitions (structs, enums). Goal: one descriptor file per system (YAML or JSON) drives the loader with zero hard-coded system knowledge in Java/Python. Output: draft schema + one worked example (e.g. SNES).
notes:
DESCRIPTOR DATA SOURCES (2026-07-03 survey):
- mist64/c64ref — canonical structured C64 reference (src/kernal/, src/c64io/, src/c64mem/); structured text + Python generator that can be adapted to emit JSON/YAML. THE upstream to consume.
- sajattack/c64-asm-labels — ready-made whole-memory-map label files in ACME/KickAssembler/radare2/VICE-.sym formats. CHECK LICENSE — derived from 'Mapping the Commodore 64' (Leemon), possible encumbrance like c64_ghidra.
- VICE .sym format ('al <hexaddr> .<label>') = de-facto C64 symbol interchange; Ghidra ImportSymbolsScript parses similar.
- KickAssembler built-in MOS6526_CIA/MOS6581_SID/MOS6569_VICII structs = cross-check for IO register offsets.
- c64-wiki Memory_Map banking table — the $0001 LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN combinations to encode as named bank configurations in the descriptor (the part no existing loader handles).
Schema implication: descriptor needs (a) regions, (b) named bank configurations selecting overlay sets, (c) symbol/label imports with provenance, (d) IO register struct definitions.
BANK-SWITCHING DESCRIPTOR DESIGN (user, 2026-07-03): decompose per-game banking info as MECHANISM + INITIAL STATE.
- C64: mechanism = write to $01; initial state = #$37 (BASIC+KERNAL+IO active, CHARROM inactive). Later add cartridge GAME/EXROM lines — note .crt header bytes 0x18/0x19 literally store EXROM/GAME line state, so for cartridges initial state can come from the container, like iNES headers do for NES.
- NES: mechanism = the Mapper (defines memory segmentation + what constitutes register reads/writes); initial state = PCB-specific -> descriptor-friendly.
- Implication for schema: MECHANISM is code-shaped (pluggable strategies — NES mappers will need several categories of register-access handling, e.g. MMC1's serial 5-write loading), INITIAL STATE is pure data. Descriptor names a mechanism + parameters + initial state; the earlier 'named bank configurations' idea becomes the STATE SPACE the mechanism transitions through.
- C64 = deliberately simple POC of the mechanism plumbing (single-register write) before NES stresses programmability.
DRAFT 1 DELIVERED (2026-07-03): ghidra/SCHEMA.md (design notes) + ghidra/descriptors/c64.yaml (worked example; YAML-validated, 8 bank states / 3 windows / 7 fixed regions).
Key schema decisions in draft:
- windows/occupants model: banked ranges declare candidate occupants; states assign occupant per window. Enumerated states table (C64: 8 PLA rows) OR mechanism-computed (NES) — schema allows both.
- context_register field links descriptor to the bundled 6510 language's bank context field (TMode-style); agreement needs a build-time check (open question 3).
- symbol sets are user-toggleable with game-RE defaults (kernal-api ON, kernal-zeropage/basic OFF since games reuse those).
- 'kind: entry' symbols create functions on EMPTY ROM slots so KERNAL calls resolve to named stubs without ROM bytes.
- descriptor states hardware facts (repeat_to mirrors); loader chooses representation.
OPEN QUESTIONS for user review (in SCHEMA.md): (1) struct source of truth: inline YAML vs c64ref-generated vs .gdt archives; (2) symbol interchange: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer, or .sym canonical; (3) descriptor<->language agreement check for context register.
TODO before close: verify ROM SHA1s against real ROM set (placeholders emptied); adapt c64ref generator for the generated/*.yaml sources; VICE cross-check of the 8-state table.
SCHEMA REVISION 1.1 (user input, 2026-07-03): READ/WRITE ASYMMETRY. Bank mapping must differentiate read vs write targets — C64 writes under BASIC/KERNAL ROM always reach the RAM beneath; $D000 varies by state (IO: r/w both chips; CHARGEN: read ROM, write RAM). Modeled as occupant property 'on_write' (not per-state): omitted=self, <occupant>=write-through, 'mechanism'=writes are bank-mechanism events (NES mapper writes — doubles as analyzer watch-list), 'none'=open bus (Ultimax later). Per-state variance falls out of occupant selection automatically.
GIB.2 IMPLICATION recorded in SCHEMA.md: Ghidra resolves references to ONE address space — LDA $A000 and STA $A000 in the same bank state cannot target different blocks. Context-aware resolution hook must be ACCESS-TYPE-AWARE: (context, address, access) -> block. Loader-policy mitigation meanwhile: analyzer annotates stores into ROM-mapped ranges with reference to on_write target.
REVIEW DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03) — SCHEMA.md open questions resolved:
(1) Structs: YAML canonical, .gdt generated at BUILD time FROM THE START (not staged via load-time builder). Loader only consumes .gdt. New bead game-music-extraction-gib.1.5 (blocks gib.1.3) for the generator + Gradle task. .gdt = build artifact, never committed; CI regenerates.
(2) Symbols: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer (community files, cc65/KickAss output).
(3) Descriptor<->language: LOAD-TIME check — loader verifies language declares banking.context_register, clear error on mismatch.
IMPLICATION flagged to user: building the Gradle/.gdt pipeline is the first real EXTENSION CODE, which per the incubation rule ('extension gets its own repo from creation time') approaches repo-birth.

title: Survey Ghidra loader/extension API and existing console loaders
description: Audit: what API surface does Ghidra expose for loaders? What existing open-source console loaders exist (NES, SNES, PS1)? Determine if extension vs. script vs. core loader plugin is the right artifact type. Survey: GhidraNES, ghidra-snes-loader, ghidra-psx-ldr, etc. Output: a short design note on the extension/loader API contract and gaps vs. our needs.
notes:
PRIOR ART SEEDS (from user, 2026-07-03):
- https://github.com/hippietrail/RetroGhidra — multi-retro-system Ghidra extension; POSSIBLE CONTRIBUTION TARGET instead of reinvention; survey must include contribute-vs-build verdict
- https://github.com/c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra — possible useful C64-specific material
- https://cesarmiquel.github.io/tech/art/science/design/2020/03/13/week-13.html — general Ghidra console-RE article, many good links
- HN 46882389 (Ghidra MCP tools) — spun off to bead game-music-extraction-gib.3
IN-TREE FINDINGS (D:/git/ghidra): 6502 + 65C02 languages exist, NO 6510 variant (identical ISA; $00/$01 port is a memory-map annotation concern, not decode). No console loaders in-tree; nearest templates: BinaryLoader, MotorolaHexLoader (opinion package).
RETROGHIDRA SURVEY VERDICT (2026-07-03): BUILD NEW, upstream shallow pieces later as goodwill.
- ~29 loaders, all uniformly SHALLOW: parse header -> createInitializedBlock -> entry point. No loader anywhere models IO registers, full hw memory maps, or banking; zero use of overlay address spaces (even Atari 2600 mirrors are just separately-named blocks).
- C64 support = thin CommodorePrgLoader.java (single CODE block, no C64 labels), C64CrtLoader.java (3 labels), D80 filesystem. No KERNAL labels, no VIC/SID/CIA, no banking.
- Architecture = one Java class per format, knowledge as Java constants; NO data-driven layer (an unused GSON GhidraLabel.java hints it was considered). Our descriptor-driven design would FIGHT their architecture, not extend it.
- Apache 2.0; alive but small (35 stars, ~4-5 contributors, bursty maintenance; Ghidra 12.x compat PR #23 open with engagement but unmerged).
- Use as REFERENCE for Ghidra API boilerplate only. After our C64 loader works, consider upstreaming format-detection pieces as standalone PR.

C64_GHIDRA SURVEY (2026-07-03): c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra has working C64BinLoader.java (PRG load-addr detection, override option, zp/stack blocks, overlay mode) and c64LabelAddrs.py (74KB comprehensive KERNAL/BASIC ROM+RAM symbol tables). NO LICENSE SPECIFIED -> cannot reuse code/data verbatim; either ask author or regenerate labels from primary sources. No banking model, no VIC/SID/CIA annotations.

GHIDRA-MCP (2026-07-03): bethington/ghidra-mcp very active, Apache 2.0, 256 tools; assumes binary already loaded, modern-platform-oriented. Useful AFTER loader works (agent-driven verification of blocks/labels). Recorded on gib.3. HN criticisms: tool-count bloat degrades LLM tool use; fork quality concerns vs LaurieWired original.
BROAD SURVEY (2026-07-03): Three memory-map patterns exist in the wild, all painful:
(1) Overlay blocks at same vaddr (fortenbt/Ghidra-SMB3INES-Loader, Dan Sanderson C64 Crossroads walkthrough) — hardware-truthful but cross-block flow analysis breaks;
(2) Separate non-overlapping blocks per bank (kylewlacy/GhidraNes, 40+ mappers) — no addr conflicts but loses runtime-address correspondence;
(3) Manual annotation after flat load (Sanderson: ~38 hand edits for a small program).
NOBODY does descriptor-driven automation — that is the confirmed gap.
Key references: SMB3 loader = best overlay+symbol-injection example (11,500 symbols); achan1989/ghidra-snes-loader = best LoROM/HiROM mirror modeling (study for SNES phase); zeroKilo/C64LoaderWV (.d64); Dan Sanderson https://dansanderson.com/mega65/crossroads-part-2/ = clearest description of the manual workflow our loader automates; retroreversing.com/ghidra = curated plugin list.
GHIDRA-C64HELPERS CONTENTS (user inspection, 2026-07-03): (a) 6510-specific processor definition — easily incorporated into our extension (extensions can bundle languages; resolves the no-6510-in-tree gap properly instead of aliasing 6502); (b) PETSCII visualizer — feeds the generalized string-detection feature (bead game-music-extraction-gib.1.4).
MIGRATION (2026-07-03): subtree migrated to CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines (this bead = grm-1.1 there). ghidra/SURVEY.md now lives at docs/SURVEY.md in that repo.
close_reason: Survey complete. Deliverable: ghidra/SURVEY.md in GME (migrates with epic). Verdict: build new extension; RetroGhidra as API reference only. Key findings: descriptor-driven automation is a confirmed empty niche; upstream banked-memory space is open with 6 motivating issues and a clear proposal shape (TMode-style context + context-aware address resolution hook); c64ref is the clean descriptor data source; 6510 language bundle-able from ghidra-c64helpers precedent.

title: Engage vgmtrans maintainers: post initiative + both RFCs for early signoff
description: Before heavy C++ work, open a GitHub discussion/issue on vgmtrans/vgmtrans summarizing the raw-disc-input initiative and the two RFCs (multi-collection architecture; per-game on-disc compression seam). Goal: secure direction/signoff on the architectural seams that are expensive to change later, and confirm appetite for upstreaming a generic PS1 disc-image loader. Capture maintainer decisions back into the RFC issues' design fields before implementation proceeds.

title: RFC: extension point for game-dependent on-disc compression/encoding
description: On-disc sound data is often compressed/encoded per game (e.g. FF7 LZS, FF9 packing) and must be decoded BEFORE the sequence can even be located/parsed -- unlike PSF where the loader already hands the scanner a flat RAM image. vgmtrans precedent is scattered: loaders decode whole files (KabukiDecrypt, CPS3Decrypt) and some scanners decode inline (TriAcePS1); there is NO general seam for pluggable per-game disc codecs. Design that seam and get maintainer signoff. OPTIONS TO PRESENT: (A) disc loader runs a per-game codec and emits already-decompressed VirtFiles (keeps scanners clean); (B) a pluggable 'disc codec/layout provider' interface keyed by game-DB entry; (C) decode inside the scanner (matches TriAcePS1 but couples codec to format). Reference implementations to port live in this repo: psx/ff7/unlzs.pl, psx/ff7/unpack_kernel_bin.pl, psx/lod/unpack.pl. Deliverable: written design note + recommended option for maintainer feedback.
notes: 2026-07-12 from 8lo.2 close-out: the compression-seam RFC now has TWO customers — FF7 LZS (field DATs) and FF8 LZ5-variant + PADBUG containers (FF8DISCn.IMG root files 0x1E-0x7F, each holding two AKAO files). Frame the RFC as a family pattern, not a one-game need. See docs/vgmtrans-disc-loader-design.md par.3/6.

title: RFC: single game image -> multiple VGMColls (multi-song architecture)
description: vgmtrans's typical input (one PSF) = one song; a disc/ROM holds many songs. Design how one image yields N playable VGMColls and get maintainer signoff BEFORE implementation. Good news: infrastructure largely exists -- the Matcher (FilegroupMatcher/GetIdMatcher/SimpleMatcher) already groups multiple seqs+instrsets+sampcolls from one scan into multiple VGMColls, and KonamiArcadeScanner already emits many sequences from one MAME romset driven by a seq_table + per-game offsets in an XML game-DB entry (getHexAttribute). PROPOSAL TO EVALUATE: reuse that pattern for discs -- a disc loader + disc-aware scanner that reads a per-game song table and emits N collections, with per-game metadata externalized (XML game-DB, mirroring this repo's akao/*.yaml). OPEN QUESTIONS for maintainers: (1) loader vs scanner vs matcher responsibility split for disc layout; (2) how a single loaded disc surfaces many collections in the UI/Root; (3) acceptable shape of a per-game disc-definition record. Deliverable: written design note posted for maintainer feedback.
notes: 2026-07-12 from 8lo.2 close-out: multi-song MECHANISM already works for AKAO (whole-file scan + id pairing); focus the RFC on surfacing/naming N collections. Key new lever: upstream PSFMetadataHints (#907) — VGMMetadataHint keyed (targetFormat, songIndex|romAddress|fileOffset|lookupKey) -> VGMTag, provider attached to RawFile; only PSFLoader populates, consumers nascent. Proposing AKAO-id -> hint wiring rides the existing upstream direction; GME YAML titles are the ready-made hint source. See docs/vgmtrans-disc-loader-design.md par.4.

title: AKAO-from-disc path: locate blocks, feed AkaoScanner, validate FF7
description: Using the mounted disc, locate AKAO sequence/sample blocks (per-game offsets/signatures from RE) and present them to the existing AkaoScanner -- either by producing a RAM-image VirtFile or invoking the scanner at known offsets. Acceptance: extracting one game (FF7) from its original disc yields VGMSeq/MIDI byte-identical (or musically identical) to the PSF-rip path established in the bootstrap issue.
notes: EARLY SIGNAL (from environment test, pre-implementation): fed a standalone extracted Chrono Cross AKAO block (z:/psx/cc/akao/02-1d15c.bin) to the freshly-built vgmtrans-cli. RESULT: AkaoScanner correctly finds the 'AKAO' signature, guessVersion->3_2, isPossibleAkaoSeq passes, parseHeader OK (track_bits 0x7fff=15 tracks, instr ptr 0x930), and the 15 track pointers are valid/in-range (track1@0x5e, then 0x603,0x64c,...). BUT VGMSeq::load() returns false -> seq not registered -> CLI reports 'not a recognized music file'. Extraction is sound; failure is in track EVENT parsing. HYPOTHESIS: vgmtrans targets PSF RAM images (block embedded in 2MB RAM); a standalone .bin that ends exactly after the instrument section (file size 0x9c0, instr@0x930) likely makes a track event-read run past EOF. IMPLICATIONS: (1) the disc loader (8lo.3) should present blocks within a larger buffer / padded region, OR ensure end-of-track handling; (2) possible CC parity nuance (cross-ref 8lo.6). For a clean PSF->AKAO BASELINE (8lo.1), use an actual PSF rip rather than a standalone block. Build/run environment itself is fully validated.

title: PS1 disc-image FileLoader (.cue/.bin/.iso) -> VirtFiles
description: New vgmtrans FileLoader that mounts a raw PS1 CD image: parse 2352-byte raw sectors + ISO9660 directory, expose contained files (EXE, overlays, sound data) as VirtFiles for downstream scanners. Port logic from this repo's psx/*/readsectors.pl, dump_iso_dir.pl, dump_path_table.pl. This is the core input-breadth deliverable and is reusable beyond AKAO. Register via LoaderRegistration; add to CMake.

title: Survey & design: PSFLoader->AkaoScanner pipeline + disc-loader contract
description: Document exactly how PSFLoader builds the PS1 RAM image and how AkaoScanner consumes a RawFile to emit VGMSeq/VGMInstrSet. Specify the minimal contract a disc-based loader must satisfy so the EXISTING AkaoScanner fires unchanged (VirtFile shape, base addresses, where it expects sequence vs sample tables). Map where AKAO data physically lives on each disc (main EXE, overlays, or standalone sound files) for FF7/FF8/FF9/Chrono Cross, drawing on this repo's psx/*/extract_akao + findakao tools. Check whether CHDLoader already provides reusable disc mounting. Output: short design doc + in-scope game list.
design:
SURVEY & DESIGN (drafted from vgmtrans + this repo's psx/ code reading; live-build validation still pending 8lo.1)

=== 1. PSFLoader -> VirtFile pipeline ===
PSFLoader.apply(RawFile) detects 'PSF'+version, builds an Image by overlay()ing the
PSF EXE (at its EXE-header load address) plus recursive _lib/_libN files, then:
  new VirtFile(img.data, img.size, name, path, tag); enqueue(virt);
The VirtFile is just the flat EXE/RAM bytes (offset 0 = lowest load addr). Tag (incl.
album) is carried from PSF metadata.

=== 2. Root chain (Root.cpp:87-125) ===
Per RawFile: run ALL LoaderManager loaders (each may enqueue VirtFiles), then run
scanners (extension-specific if any registered for the ext, else ALL scanners).
Enqueued VirtFiles recurse through the same loader+scanner path. enqueue() is the
FileLoader hook.

=== 3. AkaoScanner.scan(RawFile) ===
- version = determineVersionFromTag(file): switch on tag.album string ("Final Fantasy 7",
  "Chrono Cross", "Final Fantasy 9", ...). UNKNOWN -> per-block guessVersion().
- Byte-scans the ENTIRE file for BE 0x414B414F ("AKAO") at every offset.
  * seq_length (readShort @ off+6) != 0  -> AkaoSeq(file, off, ver); then seq->newInstrSet()
  * seq_length == 0                       -> AkaoSampColl(file, off, ver)
  id = readShort @ off+4. Seq/SampColl parse RELATIVE to their block offset in the file.
- Hard-coded FF7 hack: if size>=0x1A8000 and words@0xe0000/0x156000==0x1010, load an
  AkaoSampColl from fixed RAM offsets (the FF7 instrAll/instrDat instrument tables).
  This is exactly the kind of per-game constant this repo externalizes to YAML.
- AkaoMatcher pairs seqs<->instrSets<->sampColls BY ID into AkaoColl (its own matcher/coll,
  not the generic FilegroupMatcher).

=== 4. KEY CONCLUSION: multi-song is ALREADY solved for AKAO ===
Because the scanner byte-scans the whole image for every "AKAO" and the matcher pairs by
id, a single RawFile holding many AKAO blocks already yields many AkaoColls with NO scanner
changes. 8lo.8 (multi-song RFC) is therefore about GENERALITY/UX (other drivers, surfacing
N colls per disc), not an AKAO mechanism gap.

=== 5. DISC-LOADER CONTRACT (minimal, for unchanged AkaoScanner) ===
A disc loader must produce a RawFile/VirtFile such that:
 (a) AKAO seq + sampcoll blocks appear as CONTIGUOUS bytes (sectors cooked, archives
     unpacked, game compression decoded) -- so the signature scan + relative parse work.
 (b) tag.album set to a recognized string (clean path) OR rely on guessVersion fallback.
 (c) enqueue() it; Root auto-runs AkaoScanner; AkaoMatcher builds the collections.
Instrument/sample data that is NOT "AKAO"-tagged (FF7 instrAll/instrDat) needs explicit
per-game pointers (today: hard-coded; target: per-game config like the YAMLs).

=== 6. CHDLoader reuse ===
Only handles CHD (magic 'MComprHD'): decompresses all hunks to one flat buffer, wraps in a
single VirtFile (propagates file->tag), enqueues. Does NOT parse a filesystem. NOT directly
reusable for raw .bin/.cue/.iso, but its pattern (decode -> one VirtFile -> enqueue ->
signature scan) is the template for the "simple/cooked-image" path. The new PS1 disc loader
(8lo.3) is a sibling loader, not a CHDLoader extension.

=== 7. WHERE AKAO LIVES PER GAME (from this repo's psx tools) ===
- Chrono Cross (psx/cc/extractakao.pl): raw 2352-byte sectors; AKAO blocks span sectors and
  MUST be cooked (strip 24-byte subheader, keep 0x800 data) to become contiguous. No archive,
  no compression -> easiest once sector-cooking exists.
- FF9 (extract_akao.pl, findakao): custom archive FF9.IMG with a typed directory (DB types
  incl. 7=Song data, 9=Instrument data), 0x800 cooked sectors. Must parse FF9.IMG dir, emit
  Song/Instrument entries. findakao confirms a plain "AKAO" byte-scan finds blocks in the
  cooked image -- i.e. vgmtrans scanner works as-is on it.
- FF7 (extract_akao.pl): AKAO embedded INSIDE field-script DAT files + world-map TXZ, located
  via per-file extraOffset tables in each file's header. Field files live in the ISO9660 FS and
  are LZS-compressed -> needs FS walk + per-file decompress (psx/ff7/unlzs.pl) + offset-table
  walk. Most complex; this is the case that motivates the compression-seam RFC (8lo.9).
- FF8: not yet surveyed here; expect FF7-class complexity (own packing). Survey before scoping.

=== 8. IMPLICATION FOR 8lo.3 (disc loader) ===
Two-tier design recommended:
  Tier 1 (cooked-image path, mirrors CHDLoader): mount .cue/.bin/.iso, cook 2352->2048
  (mode2/form1, strip subheader), produce a logical image; for CC/FF9 this is enough to
  byte-scan. Reuse logic from psx/*/readsectors.pl + dump_iso_dir/path_table.
  Tier 2 (per-game extraction): ISO9660 FS walk -> locate game-specific archives/files ->
  per-game decode (FF9.IMG dir; FF7 LZS + extraOffset tables) -> emit per-file VirtFiles.
  Tier 2 is where 8lo.9 (compression seam) and 8lo.5 (per-game config) plug in.

=== 9. IN-SCOPE GAMES (difficulty order) ===
  1. Chrono Cross   - sector-cook only (lowest risk first target)
  2. FF9            - FF9.IMG archive dir parse, cooked sectors
  3. FF7            - ISO9660 + LZS decompress + embedded offset tables (needs 8lo.9)
  4. FF8            - survey first; likely FF7-class
notes: 2026-07-12 VALIDATION + FF8 SURVEY COMPLETE — deliverable at docs/vgmtrans-disc-loader-design.md (supersedes/refines the design field draft). Draft claims re-verified at fork HEAD 96840ecb (branch akao-optional-sample-collection, upstream-synced): AkaoScanner mechanics, FF7 0x1A8000/0xe0000/0x156000 hack, album-string version map all current. TWO material updates: (1) Root.cpp:106-111 — a loader that extracts ANY children sets setUseScanners(false) on the parent, so the disc loader must emit VirtFiles for ALL AKAO-bearing content (all-or-nothing contract clause); (2) NEW upstream mechanism PSFMetadataHints (#907): VGMMetadataHint/IndexedMetadataHintProvider on RawFile, keyed (targetFormat, songIndex|romAddress|fileOffset|lookupKey) -> VGMTag — the upstream-blessed channel for GME YAML per-song titles; only PSFLoader populates it so far, consumers nascent. FF8 SURVEYED (nocash + FFRTT): FF8DISCn.IMG monolith, root dir at 0h NTSC / 2800h PAL (sector+size entries, ISO-start-relative); root files 0x1E-0x7F are PADBUG archives EACH HOLDING TWO AKAO FILES (0x4B: AKAO+TXT); LZ5-variant compression; fields dir (LZS FIELD.BIN) not needed for music. FF8 is therefore FF9-class + PADBUG/LZ5 decode, EASIER than FF7 — revised difficulty order: CC, FF9, FF8, FF7. 8lo.9 gains a second customer (FF8 LZ5 alongside FF7 LZS).
close_reason: Survey & design complete: docs/vgmtrans-disc-loader-design.md — pipeline validated at fork HEAD, disc-loader contract (5 clauses incl. new all-or-nothing rule), per-game AKAO map now including FF8, revised difficulty order CC/FF9/FF8/FF7.

title: vgmtrans bootstrap: fork, build locally, confirm PSF->AKAO baseline
description: Fork vgmtrans/vgmtrans (delivery = upstream PRs). Build the project locally on this Windows/CMake setup; resolve toolchain/deps. Run it against a known FF PSF rip and confirm the existing Akao format produces correct VGMSeq/MIDI. Establishes the working baseline every later issue is validated against.
notes:
PSF->AKAO BASELINE CONFIRMED. Ran built vgmtrans-cli on M:/Music/PSFs/chronocross/'Chrono Cross 102 The Brink of Death.psf' -> 1 input, 1 output collection, exported 'Akao Seq 33'.mid (50KB) + .sf2 + .dls. Full pipeline verified: PSFLoader builds PS1 RAM image -> AkaoScanner finds seq id 0x33 + its sample collection -> AkaoMatcher forms VGMColl -> MIDI/SF2/DLS export. 
CONCLUSION on standalone extracted blocks (z:/psx/{cc,ff9}/akao/*.bin): both CC and FF9 fail identically ('not a recognized music file') -> the failure is INPUT FORM (standalone seq block lacks sample-collection + RAM context for the matcher), NOT CC-specific, NOT a parity bug, NOT environment. Confirms survey: a real loader must present seq + sampcoll blocks together in proper framing (8lo.3/8lo.4). 
8lo.1 STATUS: build DONE, PSF baseline DONE. Only remaining acceptance item = fork upstream repo, deferred until PR time (8lo.7/8lo.10). Recommend closing once fork is created, or now with fork tracked under 8lo.7.
close_reason: PSF->AKAO baseline confirmed (recorded in notes); fork confirmed to exist at D:/git/vgmtrans (origin CBongo/vgmtrans), built in VS Code. Both acceptance items met. Remaining PR-time fork/CI work tracked under 8lo.7.

title: vgmtrans: raw game-disc input loaders for AKAO games (upstream)
description: Bring raw PS1 disc-image ingestion to vgmtrans so its EXISTING Akao scanner can extract FF7/FF8/FF9/Chrono Cross directly from original discs, not just PSF rips. Reuses reverse-engineering knowledge from this repo's psx/ ISO/sector/FAT tools and akao/ YAML metadata. Pipeline: a new FileLoader mounts the disc image and emits VirtFile(s) (e.g. a PS1 RAM/EXE image); the unchanged AkaoScanner then signature-scans and builds VGMSeq/VGMInstrSet. Delivery: upstream PRs to vgmtrans/vgmtrans (match their C++ conventions). First contribution axis: INPUT LOADERS.

title: Draft upstream RFC: context-aware (bank + access-type) address resolution atop overlays
description: Write the Ghidra Discussion/RFC draft proposing first-class banked-memory support: flow-tracked bank context register (TMode-precedent UX) + a core hook from context state to memory-block/overlay selection, with access-type-aware signature (context, address, access_type) -> block to represent C64 write-under-ROM / NES PRG-ROM-read-vs-mapper-write asymmetry. Ground it in the surveyed evidence (Discussions #6651/#5913, Issues #7052/#2546/#864/#1332), the minimal-mechanism framing maintainers favored in PR #8130, and the working C64 PRG loader POC (ghidra-retro-machines) as the concrete motivating case incl. the home-in-base workaround it was forced into. Deliverable: docs/rfc-banked-memory.md in ghidra-retro-machines, reviewed by user BEFORE any upstream posting (posting is a separate, user-gated step).
notes:
DRAFT WRITTEN: D:/git/ghidra-retro-machines/docs/rfc-banked-memory.md — awaiting user review; POSTING IS USER-GATED. HOOK-POINT RESEARCH (verified vs 12.1.2 source at D:/git/ghidra; crux citations spot-checked verbatim): (Q1) ALL operand+flow addresses funnel through ONE primitive: SleighInstructionPrototype.getHandleAddr(FixedHandle,AddressSpace) @ SleighInstructionPrototype.java:1565 — builds addr from Sleigh-static hand.space; only dynamic input is curSpace (the instruction's OWN space), re-homed via curSpace.getOverlayAddress. Callers: getAddress(opIndex,ctx):788, addHandleObject:1507 (via getOpRepresentationList:767), gatherFlows:657 (flow targets). Reference materialization: CodeManager.addReferencesForInstruction @ CodeManager.java:2604 -> addDefaultMemoryReferenceIfMissing:2715. (Q2) Asymmetry cause: OverlayAddressSpace.getOverlayAddress:153 only maps base->THIS overlay; base-space instructions never resolve into overlays; overlay A never resolves into overlay B. (Q3) Context register value IS in scope one frame up: getAddress holds SleighParserContext (line 796, packed context bits = bank state) — just not threaded into getHandleAddr. TMode (ARM.sinc:88-91) influences DECODE only; nothing analogous touches address resolution. (Q4) Access type already computed at same layer: RefTypeFactory.getDefaultMemoryRefType @ RefTypeFactory.java:398 (from CodeManager.getOperandMemoryReferenceType:2775) distinguishes READ/WRITE via p-code input/result objects -> hook CAN be access-type-aware. (Q5) In-tree half-precedents: InjectPayloadSegment (segmentop: register value participates in addr computation), SegmentedAddressSpace (addressing = f(segment)), VarnodeContext (register->space tracking along flow, overlay-aware ~line 237), DisassemblerContextImpl/ProgramContext (flow-tracked context persistence). STORAGE ALREADY PERMITS cross-space refs: ReferenceDBManager.addMemoryReference:422 checks only isMemoryAddress on both ends — interim analyzer-created refs into overlays are legal today. RFC ASK distilled: thread SleighParserContext + RefType into getHandleAddr (or overload); selection = resolve(context,address,access_type)->block via declarative bank map; falls back to today's behavior when unmapped.
EXECUTE-MODE DECISION (user question, 2026-07-05): in the general case EXECUTE routes like READ — 6502-family banking hardware (C64 PLA, NES mappers) sees only address + R/W line; SYNC/fetch is not routed, so fetch is electrically a read. Bank map schema therefore defaults execute->read mapping, NO third column in the common case. But hook signature KEEPS access_type ∈ {READ, WRITE, EXECUTE} because: (1) free — flow targets (gatherFlows) vs data operands (RefTypeFactory) already arrive distinguished; collapsing is extra work; (2) fetch-sensitive hardware exists (Z80 M1: Sega MC-8123, Capcom Kabuki decrypt opcodes differently from data at same addr) -> optional per-window execute override stays representable; (3) policy asymmetry — wrong flow resolution poisons disassembly, wrong data ref is just an imprecise xref, so impl may demand higher context confidence for EXECUTE. ANALYZER COMPAT (user's main concern, branch-into-non-X heuristics): VERIFIED compose cleanly — Disassembler.getInitializedMemory (Disassembler.java:309) filters block.isInitialized() && block.isExecute() (line 411) on the block the target LANDS in, i.e. AFTER resolution; context-aware routing makes the suspect-branch check MORE accurate AND finer-grained. Worked example (user-corrected: CHARGEN is glyph data, not executable — reference the all-RAM state for the unflagged case): JMP $D000 → all-RAM state: executable RAM, unflagged; IO state: non-X IO block, flagged; CHARGEN state: font ROM (descriptor marks non-X), flagged. Unmapped context falls back to status quo. RFC updated with 'Is EXECUTE a real third mode' subsection.
close_reason: RFC drafted, user-reviewed (execute-mode + phasing clarifications incorporated), and POSTED by user 2026-07-05: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/discussions/9349 — source of record remains docs/rfc-banked-memory.md in ghidra-retro-machines (substantive revisions to be mirrored to the discussion). title: POC: C64 loader that maps banked RAM/ROM, IO ports, and PRG load address
description: Implement a minimal proof-of-concept Ghidra loader for the Commodore 64 that (a) reads a PRG file's 2-byte load-address header and places code correctly, (b) maps the banked memory layout — RAM under KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN, plus the IO region — using Ghidra overlay address spaces to represent the overlapping banks selectable via the $00/$01 processor port, (c) annotates IO chip registers (VIC-II, SID, CIA1, CIA2, color RAM), (d) applies initial struct/label definitions for known hardware registers. Validates that the system descriptor design (gib.1.2) is sufficient to drive real C64 analysis. Open question to resolve in design: how faithfully to model banking given Ghidra's static memory model.
notes:
DECIDED (2026-07-03): banking fidelity question resolved — use overlay address spaces (option b). Rationale: loader-code RE needs KERNAL/BASIC visibility alongside RAM-under-ROM; overlays are Ghidra's current ceiling, and their pain points feed the core banked-memory proposal (see gib parent's core-contribution bead).
6510 language: rather than targeting 6502:LE:16:default, the extension can BUNDLE a 6510 processor definition (precedent: grue74/ghidra-c64helpers fork has one; extensions may ship data/languages). A proper 6510 language is also the natural home for the bank-context pseudo-register (see gib.2 TMode note) since $00/$01 are on-die.

title: EXTENSION INCUBATOR: Game System Architecture Loader
description:
Incubator for a Ghidra extension (loader module) that sets up a complete game system architecture in one step: maps ROM from cartridge/disc, BIOS/console ROM, RAM regions, IO port ranges, and populates initial data structure definitions so analysts start from a fully annotated memory map rather than a flat binary.

INITIAL TARGET: Commodore 64 (directly supports this repo's c64/ music RE work: acs, kik, rds). C64 is a rich first case — banked memory (/usr/bin/bash1 processor port swaps RAM/KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN/IO at overlapping addresses), well-documented IO chips (VIC-II $D000, SID $D400, CIA1 $DC00, CIA2 $DD00, color RAM $D800), and PRG load-address headers. Later targets: NES, SNES, PS1.

Publishable extension — will get its own GitHub repo and invite collaborators when ready.

MIGRATION NOTE: This epic is a self-contained subtree. When the extension repo is created, migrate with:
  bd export | grep <epic-id> | bd import  (in new repo)
  bd rename-prefix game-music-extraction <new-prefix>
Keep all dependency edges INTERNAL to this epic to avoid dangling refs after migration. Cross-epic links (to GME-internal beads) should be avoided here.

Fork clone for Ghidra dev: D:/git/ghidra (master checked out).
notes:
ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03):
1. MVP input format: PRG (2-byte load address header).
2. Banking: overlay address spaces for MVP — best Ghidra can do today. IO region always needed by music code; BASIC/KERNAL/CHARGEN rarely needed by music code itself but frequently involved in the LOADER code paths (esp. KERNAL). Long-term: improving Ghidra core banked-memory support is a stated motivation of this whole effort — see bead game-music-extraction-gib.2.
3. ROMs (copyright): symbol-only labels by default (e.g. KERNAL entry points); reserve labeled memory-map slots so users can pull their own ROM dumps in via File > Add To Program; optional loader ROM-path options possible later.
4. Schema: evolving descriptor schema from day one, NOT hardcode-C64-first. Solo development until project is more baked; collaborators later.
5. Build-vs-contribute still open pending RetroGhidra survey (gib.1.1).
REPO NAME DECIDED (user, 2026-07-03): ghidra-retro-machines. Verified collision-free on GitHub (no exact match; no confusable neighbor in the Ghidra/RE space). Pitch: 'give Ghidra the whole machine, not just the file' — descriptor-driven system architecture loaders for retro computers and consoles. Layout affordance: machines/c64.yaml, machines/nes.yaml. title: POC: re-extract AKAO instrument/sample blocks via existing psx scripts, feed full triple to vgmtrans
description: Test of Strategy B from 6pf using REAL sample data rather than loosening the matcher. Most PSX RE already located instrument+sample AKAO blocks, but only SEQUENCE blocks were left on disk (z:/psx/{cc,ff9,ff7}/akao/*.bin are seq-only; no instr/samp artifacts found). RESULT: YES — removing the sample requirement makes standalone seq blocks export MIDI. PROVEN EMPIRICALLY on the D: fork.
PATCH (3 surgical edits, AkaoMatcher.cpp::tryCreateCollection, uncommitted in D:/git/vgmtrans working tree):

title: Seq-only extraction: decouple AKAO sequence output from sample-data presence in vgmtrans
description: vgmtrans's AkaoMatcher (confirmed in 8lo.1) refuses to emit output for a standalone AKAO sequence block: it requires a matching sample-collection + RAM context to form a VGMColl, so a bare seq fails with 'not a recognized music file'. Our focus is the SEQUENCE side (MIDI / score / disassembly), where instrument samples are irrelevant to the note data. Goal: let vgmtrans produce a VGMSeq/MIDI from an AKAO seq even when no sample/instrument set is found, easing the apparent hard requirement on sample data. This unblocks extracting from the standalone seq blocks we already have (z:/psx/{cc,ff9}/akao/*.bin) and from disc inputs where we have not yet located/loaded samples.
design:
Two complementary strategies, pick per investigation in 8lo.2:
STRATEGY A (ease the restriction): allow the matcher/collection step to emit a seq-only VGMColl when no AkaoSampColl/InstrSet is present. Investigate where AkaoMatcher gates on the sample collection and whether a 'sequence-only' VGMColl (no InstrSet) is acceptable to the MIDI exporter (which needs only the seq). Prefer a minimal, upstream-acceptable toggle (e.g. a scanner/loader option 'allow seq without samples') over removing the pairing logic, so existing PSF behavior is unchanged.
STRATEGY B (supply the samples from RE knowledge): we usually KNOW from reverse engineering where sample data lives and how it is loaded, even though sequence work rarely needed it. Where samples ARE wanted (SF2/DLS export), feed the matcher the correct sampcoll location/framing via game metadata (akao/ YAML) so a normal VGMColl forms. This is the richer path but requires modeling sample load addresses.
Relationship: A is the fast enabler for sequence-only goals; B reuses RE knowledge for full collections. Both feed the disc-loader path (8lo.3/8lo.4) and parity work (8lo.6).
acceptance_criteria: A built vgmtrans (or fork) produces a correct .mid from at least one standalone AKAO seq block (e.g. a CC or FF9 z:/psx/.../akao/*.bin) with NO sample collection present, where today it fails with 'not a recognized music file'. PSF baseline (8lo.1) still produces identical seq+samples output (no regression). Approach documented as a candidate upstream change (option/flag, not a behavior break).
notes:
WORKING CLONE = D:/git/vgmtrans (CBongo fork, built in VS Code), NOT z: (upstream test clone). All line numbers below verified identical on D: @ caeb9798.
SOURCE INVESTIGATION. Two independent gates; requirement is NOT AKAO-specific:
GATE 1 collection formation: AkaoMatcher::tryCreateCollection (AkaoMatcher.cpp:90) hard-requires seq+instrSet+non-empty sampColls (and line 154 matchingSampColls.size()>0 before building coll). But SimpleMatcher.h:45 (most formats) still requires a matching InstrSet even when bRequiresSampColl=false. => NO path forms a VGMColl from a bare seq; 'lone seq yields nothing' is architectural/general, AKAO just stricter.
GATE 2 export: CLIVGMRoot::exportAllCollections (CLIVGMRoot.cpp:145) iterates vgmColls() ONLY; unmatched seqs invisible -> 'not a recognized music file' (line 78) = zero COLLECTIONS formed.
KEY: conversion already supports seq-only MIDI. VGMSeq::saveAsMidi(path, coll=nullptr) (VGMSeq.h:103); saveMidi only checks coll->seq()!=nullptr (CLIVGMRoot.cpp:159/162). Samples/instrset matter only for SF2/DLS. Engine can already do this; nothing tracks/exports orphan seqs.
REVISED STRATEGY (supersedes earlier A/B framing):
  A (quick PoC, AKAO-only): patch AkaoMatcher to emit seq-only VGMColl. Works w/ today's CLI but fabricates instrument-less coll; maintainers may balk. See PoC b8q.
  B (RECOMMENDED, principled): export orphan/unmatched VGMSeqs as MIDI at Root/CLI level. Format-agnostic, reuses saveAsMidi(coll=nullptr), doesn't distort collection model. Natural home of the loosening.
  C: seq-only mode in matcher framework - more invasive, likely unnecessary given B.
RELATED PoCs: b8q (strip matcher / seq-only), hbt (re-extract real instr+samp blocks via psx scripts, feed full triple).

title: Tier A: externalize FF7 hard-coded scanner constants -> data-driven AKAO game-DB entry
description: Replace vgmtrans's hard-coded FF7 handling with per-game DATA, mirroring the existing MAME XML game-DB pattern (KonamiArcadeScanner reads seq_table/samp_tables via getHexAttribute). Concretely externalize: (1) AkaoScanner's hard-coded AkaoInstrDatLocation(0xe0000,0x156000,0,128) + 0x1A8000/0x1010 magic; (2) determineVersionFromTag's album->version switch; (3) optional song id->title naming (today auto-named 'Akao Seq {id}'). This is the data half of this repo's ff7.yaml. IMPORTANT: externalization is REQUIRED for the disc path, not just cleanup -- on a real disc the RAM-image offsets 0xe0000/0x156000 are meaningless; you have ISO9660/archive offsets that must come from per-game data. Idiomatic and maintainer-friendly given the MAME precedent. Effort: moderate (struct + lookup + scanner refactor).
design: Decomposition of porting this repo's config-driven AKAO strategy into vgmtrans. TIER A (this issue) = externalize per-game CONSTANTS/locations into a game-DB record. Idiomatic: MAME loader already does XML game-DB (getHexAttribute). Required for disc loading (8lo.3/8lo.5) because RAM-image offsets don't exist on disc. Maps to ff7.yaml's instrument-location + version + songs fields. Keep the hand-written AkaoSeq parser (that's Tier C).

title: AKAO Seq parity gaps: diff Python opcode handling vs vgmtrans AkaoSeq
description: Compare this repo's akao/ Python opcode/event handling (ir_events.py, format_psx.py) against vgmtrans's AkaoSeq to find opcodes/variants vgmtrans mis-handles or omits (e.g. Chrono Cross specifics, volume/expression mapping). File concrete parity fixes against upstream AkaoSeq. Independent of the loader work; can proceed in parallel after the survey.
notes: FIRST CONCRETE PARITY FINDING (empirical, via vgmtrans-cli on real Chrono Cross AKAO data): vgmtrans AkaoSeq emits 'Unknown Event 0xFE 0x13' and the track parse derails. ROOT CAUSE: vgmtrans's hand-written event map lacks 0xFE13. This repo's akao/chrono_cross.yaml ALSO marks 0xFE13 semantic=unknown -- BUT with params:0, i.e. it knows the OPERAND LENGTH even without the semantic, so the Python parser skips it and continues. LESSON (the core parity-robustness pattern): for not breaking, operand LENGTHS matter more than semantics. ACTION for vgmtrans: audit AkaoSeq's FE-subcode handling against this repo's fe_opcode_table (format_psx.py fe_oplen + chrono_cross/ff8/ff9 yaml) and add missing subcodes (0xFE13 and others in 0x08-0x1F range) with correct lengths even when semantics are unknown, so unknown-but-known-length opcodes don't abort the track. This is also the strongest concrete motivation for Tier C (8lo.13): a data-driven opcode-LENGTH table is what makes parsing robust. Also seen: standalone/concatenated seq blocks produce 0 MIDI output because the CLI exports matched VGMColls (seq+sampcoll paired by id); sample-collection AKAO blocks (seq_length==0) must be present+matched -- cross-ref 8lo.4.

title: Generalized string detection: PETSCII + per-game tile-table text mappings
description:
Future feature: extend string detection beyond ASCII for retro systems.
- C64: PETSCII (KERNAL/CHROUT strings) AND screen codes (direct screen-RAM writes) — two DIFFERENT mappings, each with shifted/unshifted charset variants. Prior art: PETSCII visualizer in grue74/ghidra-c64helpers fork (inspect for reuse ideas).
- NES/SNES: per-game tile->character mappings, published as .tbl 'table files' by the ROM-hacking/translation community (romhacking.net, Data Crystal) — a de-facto standard format we could ingest directly, giving per-game string detection from community-documented data.
Integration points to investigate: Ghidra string data types support pluggable Java Charsets (extension could register PETSCII charsets); string-search analyzer charset hooks; descriptor schema could reference charset/table per system or per game.
Fits the descriptor-driven vision: text encoding is system knowledge (or game knowledge, for tile tables) that belongs in data, not code.

Hard part is not the mechanism but choosing correct strategy per game -- defer until selection criteria are characterized (feeds from 8lo.6 parity analysis).

Until then, this repo's opcode YAML is used only as a reference spec to fix parity bugs (see 8lo.6), not as runtime config. Deliverable: a written proposal/RFC framing the merge and its tradeoffs for maintainer discussion.
design: TIER C of the strategy-port decomposition. NOT recommended as a wholesale port (would replace a working 1598-line parser; divergent from vgmtrans norms => likely 'no'). Owner frames it as merging techniques + major refactor needing maintainer discussion first. Gate behind maintainer engagement (8lo.10). Reference-only use of opcode YAML in the meantime via 8lo.6.
